subject: How does inla.mesh.1d bin time between knots

messages.author: 399bf2e734c020dc
messages.subject: How does inla.mesh.1d bin time between knots
parts:
Hi everyone,

I have 21 years of data from 2000 - 2020 that I want to divide into 7 groups of three

I have code 

gtime <- as.integer(seq(2000, 2020, length = 7))

> gtime
[1] 2000 2003 2006 2010 2013 2016 2020

mesh.t <- inla.mesh.1d(loc=gtime, degree = 1)

will the first group be 2000, 2001 and 2002 etc. ?

Many thanks,

Sylvan

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How does inla.mesh.1d bin time between knots
parts:
By default, inla.mesh.1d defines a piecewise linear basis system, so it does not "group" the time points. Instead, it defines a piecewise linear function with nodes at the input "loc" values (or "knots").
So in your example, 2000 will be mapped to the first node, 2001 will be mapped to 2/3 times the first node value plus 1/3 times the second node value, etc.

Finn
